title: The Aerospace Compounder That Turned FAA Red Tape Into a $38 Billion Business
subtitle: HEICO has compounded at 22% annually since 1990 — here's what makes its moat nearly unbreakable.
sections_used: The Moat: Regulatory Red Tape as Superpower
The Bull Case: A Berkshire Playbook in Aerospace
Where Smart Money Is Paying Attention
body_json: {"type": "doc", "content": [{"type": "paragraph", "content": [{"type": "text", "text": "Episode: ", "marks": [{"type": "italic"}]}, {"type": "text", "text": "Heico: The Quiet Aerospace Compounder", "marks": [{"type": "link", "attrs": {"href": "https://www.theinvestorspodcast.com/episodes/heico-the-quiet-aerospace-compounder/", "target": "_blank"}}]}, {"type": "text", "text": " \u2014 17 July 2025", "marks": [{"type": "italic"}]}]}, {"type": "horizontal_rule"}, {"type": "paragraph", "content": [{"type": "text", "text": "\"A $10,000 investment back in 1990 would be worth over $9 million today.\" That's how Clay Finck opens this episode \u2014 and it's not a typo. HEICO (HEI) has delivered 22% annual returns for over three decades, in what most investors would write off as a boring, commoditized aerospace parts business. Clay calls it \"one of the strongest moats I've ever studied.\" After this episode, you'll understand why."}]}, {"type": "heading", "attrs": {"level": 2}, "content": [{"type": "text", "text": "TL;DR"}]}, {"type": "paragraph", "content": [{"type": "text", "text": "HEICO is an aerospace parts supplier that has quietly outperformed nearly every major index for 35 years. Under the Mendelson family \u2014 who took the helm in 1990 \u2014 the company grew from a struggling parts distributor into a $38 billion industry leader. Its edge: FAA regulations that most companies treat as a compliance burden became HEICO's highest barrier to entry. Warren Buffett initiated a position in Q2 2024. Legendary investor Francois Rochon holds it as a core position. This is a business that rewards patience over precision."}]}, {"type": "heading", "attrs": {"level": 2}, "content": [{"type": "text", "text": "The Business: Replacement Parts No One Wants to Think About"}]}, {"type": "paragraph", "content": [{"type": "text", "text": "HEICO operates in a niche most investors skip past: replacement parts for commercial aircraft. Airlines historically had no choice but to buy these parts directly from original equipment manufacturers (OEMs) \u2014 Boeing, Pratt & Whitney, GE \u2014 at OEM prices. HEICO found a different path. It produces FAA-approved alternative parts (called PMA parts, for Parts Manufacturer Approval) at meaningful discounts to OEM pricing."}]}, {"type": "paragraph", "content": [{"type": "text", "text": "The result is an airline cost-saving tool that comes with full regulatory blessing. HEICO became the trusted alternative \u2014 and then locked in customers through proven reliability and relationships that make switching genuinely painful. Airlines don't experiment with aircraft components."}]}, {"type": "paragraph", "content": [{"type": "text", "text": "The business runs across two main segments: the Flight Support Group (aftermarket parts and MRO services) and the Electronic Technologies Group (defense and aerospace electronics). Both carry high switching costs, long customer relationships, and predictable recurring revenue. The episode notes that HEICO's products and services are \"extremely sticky\" \u2014 not marketing language, just physics."}]}, {"type": "heading", "attrs": {"level": 2}, "content": [{"type": "text", "text": "The Moat: Regulatory Red Tape as Superpower"}]}, {"type": "paragraph", "content": [{"type": "text", "text": "This is the counterintuitive heart of the HEICO story: FAA regulations don't slow HEICO down \u2014 they protect it."}]}, {"type": "paragraph", "content": [{"type": "text", "text": "Getting FAA approval for a PMA part is expensive, time-consuming, and technically demanding. For each individual component, HEICO must demonstrate airworthiness through rigorous documentation and testing \u2014 essentially building a certification file from scratch. Most would-be competitors look at that process and walk away. HEICO has built an internal machine for doing exactly this, over and over, across thousands of part numbers."}]}, {"type": "paragraph", "content": [{"type": "text", "text": "Once an approval is in place, it's highly durable. New entrants face the same gauntlet. Airlines, meanwhile, have every incentive to stay with a proven certified supplier they already trust \u2014 because the downside of a parts failure is catastrophic. As Clay puts it, Heico \"turned strict FAA regulations into its biggest competitive advantage.\" In a world where most moats erode, this one tends to deepen."}]}, {"type": "heading", "attrs": {"level": 2}, "content": [{"type": "text", "text": "The Bull Case: A Berkshire Playbook in Aerospace"}]}, {"type": "paragraph", "content": [{"type": "text", "text": "Three Mendelsons run the company: Lawrence (executive chairman), and brothers Victor and Eric (co-CEOs). Combined, they own over 9 million shares worth more than $2.1 billion \u2014 serious skin in the game for a family that's been at the wheel for 35 years."}]}, {"type": "paragraph", "content": [{"type": "text", "text": "HEICO's acquisition strategy looks a lot like Berkshire Hathaway's: acquire smaller niche businesses in adjacent aerospace markets, leave founders in place, preserve cultures, and provide capital access without imposing bureaucracy. The episode highlights a remarkable outcome of this model \u2014 HEICO's ownership culture has created \"hundreds of millionaire factory workers\" through long-term equity participation at all levels of the company."}]}, {"type": "paragraph", "content": [{"type": "text", "text": "There's also a structural hedge baked in: HEICO's business is countercyclical in useful ways. When airlines are under financial pressure, their incentive to switch from expensive OEM parts to HEICO's certified alternatives increases. The worse the aviation macro environment, the more compelling HEICO's value proposition. Most industrial companies lack this property."}]}, {"type": "heading", "attrs": {"level": 2}, "content": [{"type": "text", "text": "Where Smart Money Is Paying Attention"}]}, {"type": "paragraph", "content": [{"type": "text", "text": "Warren Buffett and Berkshire Hathaway began purchasing HEICO shares in Q2 2024, building a $245 million position \u2014 what Clay calls \"really a rounding error\" for Berkshire. The signal isn't the size. It's that Buffett, who has evaluated tens of thousands of businesses over six decades, chose this one. Francois Rochon, whom Clay interviewed earlier this year and who runs one of the best long-term track records in the business, holds HEICO as a core position."}]}, {"type": "paragraph", "content": [{"type": "text", "text": "HEICO trades at an elevated valuation \u2014 the market is not asleep. But the history of compounders with durable moats, disciplined capital allocation, and aligned ownership is that paying a fair price and waiting tends to work out better than waiting for a bargain that never arrives. The question is whether the moat continues to widen. HEICO's 35-year track record and the structural advantages in its certification engine suggest it does."}]}, {"type": "horizontal_rule"}, {"type": "paragraph", "content": [{"type": "text", "text": "Books & resources mentioned:", "marks": [{"type": "bold"}]}]}, {"type": "bullet_list", "content": [{"type": "list_item", "content": [{"type": "paragraph", "content": [{"type": "text", "text": "Lessons from the Titans"}, {"type": "text", "text": " (mentioned in show notes)"}]}]}, {"type": "list_item", "content": [{"type": "paragraph", "content": [{"type": "text", "text": "Interview with Eric Mendelson", "marks": [{"type": "link", "attrs": {"href": "https://www.theinvestorspodcast.com/", "target": "_blank"}}]}, {"type": "text", "text": " (linked in show notes)"}]}]}, {"type": "list_item", "content": [{"type": "paragraph", "content": [{"type": "text", "text": "50x Podcast with Nick Howley", "marks": [{"type": "link", "attrs": {"href": "https://www.theinvestorspodcast.com/", "target": "_blank"}}]}, {"type": "text", "text": " \u2014 HEICO background"}]}]}]}, {"type": "paragraph", "content": [{"type": "text", "text": "Original podcast: ", "marks": [{"type": "italic"}]}, {"type": "text", "text": "The Investor's Podcast Network", "marks": [{"type": "link", "attrs": {"href": "https://www.theinvestorspodcast.com/", "target": "_blank"}}]}, {"type": "text", "text": " \u2014 episode 72, 17 July 2025.", "marks": [{"type": "italic"}]}]}]}
